newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Appeals Court sets Conrail argument.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Appeals Court sets Conrail argument.

text.p: The U.S. Third Circuit Court of Appeals has scheduled arguments for 3:00 p.m. Eastern Standard Time on Wednesday/1800 GMT on a request by Norfolk Southern Corp to block a Conrail sharehoders meeting Friday, a court official said.

The court is considering Norfolk Southern's request for an injunction to block a key vote on Conrail's intended merger with CSX Corp, pending resolution of Norfolk Southern's appeal challenging the merger agreement between Conrail and CSX.
A U.S. District Court judge last week upheld a provision in the agreement which forbids either Conrail or CSX from discussing a merger with a third party until 1999.

The judge also ruled CSX had not triggered a Pennsylvania law that would have required it to pay cash for the remaining 80 percent of Conrail shares it did not now own. The Conrail vote Friday is on whether to waive the law to allow the cash-and-stock merger with CSX to proceed.

In documents filed Monday with the court, Conrail said Norfolk Southern could not show any harm if the vote were to take place as scheduled Friday, but that if the vote were postponed, any delay in the merger could harm Conrail and CSX shippers, customers, employees and other "constituencies."
Norfolk Southern has said the two-year exclusivity period unfairly deprives shareholders of the opportunity to choose its own rival offer.
